Subject: Acme POC: Next steps & success criteria

Alex — great conversation earlier today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the POC: 

Summary of need:
- Acme wants to add a low-latency assistant into the Support UI that can surface KB answers and surface suggested replies.
- Key constraints: sub-200ms median token latency for streaming replies, predictable cost under projected 10k monthly active users, and enterprise data residency.

Proposed POC (4 weeks):
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria, get SOW signed, grant Redwood test API keys and access to a staging dataset (sample KB dump).
2) Week 1: integration + initial validation (SDK + API route integration, basic streaming).
3) Week 2: quality tuning and tool-calling for KB retrieval, add prefix caching for common queries.
4) Week 3: load validation, cost run-rate estimate, highlight regressions.
5) Week 4: handoff + playbook for production rollout.

Success criteria (ask to confirm):
- Functional: assistant answers correctly on the provided 200 prompt eval set with >85% accuracy.
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency <350ms, median token latency <200ms for streaming flows.
- Cost: projected unit cost <$0.0025 per generated token equivalent at expected QPS.
- Ops: logs/audit events delivered to Acme's SIEM; RBAC configured for 3 admin users.

Ownership / asks from Acme:
- Confirm success criteria above (reply inline).
- Provide a staging KB export (S3 link) and an integration technical contact for the Node.js backend (Carlos ran the call — can you confirm his email to loop him in?).
- Sign the attached POC-SOW.pdf and return (DocuSign link also available).

Deliverables from Redwood:
- Integration guide and SDK examples (Node.js + Python).
- Test harness for evaluation set + sample metrics dashboard.
- Weekly sync and a final runbook.

I attached the draft POC-SOW.pdf for legal/PM review. If this looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff for Monday (next week) and loop in Priya to lead the integration work.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Hi Alex / Carlos — Priya from Redwood engineering here. Short technical plan and what we’ll deliver for Week 1 integration: 

1) SDK + auth:
- We recommend using the Redwood Node SDK (npm package @redwood-inference/sdk). For server-side flows (Node 18), use the server streaming API to minimize end-to-end latency.
- Auth: We'll issue a scoped API key for the Acme staging project. For production you can plug an HMAC token through your KMS.

2) API routes and examples (will put in Drive):
- POST /v1/generate (server-side) — streaming token-by-token responses; best for live assistant flows.
- POST /v1/chat (structured assistant) — supports tool calling (KB retrieval) and function-like responses.
- POST /v1/embeddings — for KB indexing and similarity search.

3) Streaming recommendation:
- Use server-side streaming to the browser via server-sent events (SSE) or a WebSocket proxy to avoid exposing API keys. We will include a sample Next.js serverless route that acts as a streaming proxy.

4) Tool calling and retrieval:
- Pattern: frontend -> server proxy -> Redwood chat API with tool-callback to your KB retrieval endpoint. We support synchronous tool calling (HTTP) and an async webhook pattern if you prefer.
- We'll provide a retrieval lambda example (Node) that queries your similarity index and returns top-N results as tool outputs.

5) Performance knobs:
- KV cache for frequent prompt prefixes (we can prewarm for common support flows).
- Batching: we’ll recommend per-route batching settings to keep tail latency bounded.
- Quantization: for local dev we can provide a smaller quantized model if you want to run small evaluations on prem.

Deliverables (Week 1):
- integration-checklist.md (attached) 
- Node.js sample repo with SDK usage, streaming proxy, and tool-calling example
- A small test harness (200-prompt eval runner) + instructions to upload results to the shared Drive.

Proposed kickoff: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:00 AM PT — 30m tech sync to go through the sample repo and confirm access. If that works I’ll send the calendar invite and a short agenda.

--
Priya Natarajan

2) Data retention — for the POC we want logs kept for 30 days and not used for model training. Can you confirm Redwood supports a no-training clause for POC data?
3) Sample requests/responses — can you share a minimal streaming request and the expected SSE frame format? That will help our frontend devs.

We’ll be on the kickoff at 10:00 PT.
